title: Programmable High-dimensional State Synthesis Through A 20-m Multimode Fiber Via Long-coherence Atomic Photons
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 18 October 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates programmable synthesis and transmission of high-dimensional quantum states through a 20-m multimode fiber using long-coherence photons from atomic ensembles.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum states can enhance information capacity and noise resilience in quantum networks, but transmitting them through multimode fiber while preserving coherence is challenging.
method: The work uses long-coherence atomic photons and programmable wavefront/modulation control to synthesize high-dimensional states and propagate them through a 20-m multimode fiber.
result: The authors achieve programmable high-dimensional state synthesis and fiber transmission with maintained coherence, demonstrating a viable multimode-fiber interface for atomic-photon-based quantum states.
conclusion: This provides a promising route toward high-dimensional quantum communication and networking over multimode fiber using long-coherence atomic photon sources.

title: Genuine Continuous Quantumness
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 October 2026;
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes a notion of genuine continuous quantumness for continuous-variable quantum systems.
motivation: Continuous-variable systems require quantumness criteria that go beyond standard discrete-variable or simple nonclassicality witnesses.
method: The authors develop a framework for identifying quantumness in continuous-variable states and apply it to characterize when the quantumness is genuinely continuous rather than reducible to simpler classical or discrete descriptions.
result: They provide criteria and examples showing that certain continuous-variable states exhibit genuine continuous quantumness under the proposed definition.
conclusion: The work offers a conceptual and practical tool for certifying continuous-variable quantum resources, with relevance to quantum information processing and nonclassicality characterization.

title: Structural Control Of Two-level Defect Density Revealed By High-throughput Correlative Measurements Of Josephson Junctions
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 October 2026;
tldr: The paper uses high-throughput correlative measurements of Josephson junctions to show how structural properties control two-level defect density in superconducting qubit hardware.
motivation: Two-level-system defects in Josephson junctions are a major source of decoherence and loss in superconducting quantum circuits, so understanding and controlling their density is important for improving qubit performance.
method: The authors perform high-throughput correlative measurements on Josephson junctions, linking structural characterization to measured two-level defect densities across devices or fabrication conditions.
result: They identify structural factors that correlate with and can be used to control two-level defect density in Josephson junctions.
conclusion: The work provides a characterization-driven route toward lower-loss superconducting qubit platforms by suppressing TLS defects through structural and fabrication control.

title: Exponential Advantage In Continuous-variable Quantum State Learning
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 12 October 2026;
tldr: The paper reports an exponential advantage for learning continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Efficiently learning and characterizing continuous-variable quantum states is challenging because of their infinite-dimensional state space and the high cost of tomography.
method: It develops a quantum learning protocol or algorithm for continuous-variable states and compares its performance against classical or conventional learning strategies.
result: The work demonstrates an exponential separation in learning performance for continuous-variable quantum states.
conclusion: The results advance quantum state learning in continuous-variable systems, though they are not directly centered on the researcher's core interests in entanglement, nonlocality, entropy, or quantum thermodynamics.

title: A Quantitative Model For Embedding Quantum-secure Communications And Evaluating Communication Autonomy In Industrial Control Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 12 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a quantitative model for integrating quantum-secure communications into industrial control systems and assessing communication autonomy.
motivation: Industrial control systems require secure and autonomous communication, and quantum-secure methods may offer long-term security guarantees.
method: The authors develop a modeling framework to embed quantum-secure communication technologies and evaluate autonomy metrics in industrial control settings.
result: The model provides a way to quantify communication autonomy when quantum-secure links are deployed in industrial control architectures.
conclusion: The work is an applied system-level modeling study rather than a fundamental quantum networking or information-theoretic contribution.

title: High-order Magnus Expansion For Hamiltonian Simulation
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 October 2026;
tldr: The paper develops high-order Magnus expansion methods for Hamiltonian simulation.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation, especially for time-dependent Hamiltonians, requires accurate and efficient high-order numerical integrators.
method: It constructs and analyzes high-order Magnus expansion schemes for simulating Hamiltonian dynamics.
result: The proposed high-order methods improve simulation accuracy and scaling compared with lower-order approaches.
conclusion: The work is a useful quantum-algorithms/numerical-analysis contribution but is peripheral to the researcher's information-theoretic and thermodynamic interests.

title: Mirror Subspace Diagonalization: A Real-time Quantum Krylov Algorithm With Near-optimal Sampling Cost
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 October 2026;
tldr: The paper introduces mirror subspace diagonalization, a real-time quantum Krylov algorithm for diagonalizing quantum systems with near-optimal sampling cost.
motivation: Quantum Krylov subspace methods are promising for estimating eigenstates and eigenvalues on quantum computers, but existing approaches can suffer from high sampling overhead.
method: The authors propose a real-time quantum Krylov algorithm, called mirror subspace diagonalization, that constructs a subspace from real-time evolved states and diagonalizes it to extract eigenpairs while optimizing measurement/sampling cost.
result: The algorithm achieves near-optimal sampling cost for subspace diagonalization, improving the practical feasibility of quantum Krylov methods.
conclusion: Mirror subspace diagonalization provides an efficient real-time quantum Krylov approach with favorable sampling complexity, useful for quantum simulation and eigenvalue estimation on quantum devices.

title: Demonstration Of Subspace-search Variational Quantum Eigensolver Using Photonic Orbital Angular Momentum Qudits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 October 2026;
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a subspace-search variational quantum eigensolver using photonic orbital angular momentum qudits.
motivation: Variational quantum eigensolvers are promising for near-term quantum simulation, and qudits may offer larger state spaces per carrier; photonic orbital angular momentum provides a platform for such qudit-based algorithms.
method: The authors implement a subspace-search variational quantum eigensolver on a photonic platform encoding quantum information in orbital angular momentum qudits, using variational circuits to search targeted eigenspaces.
result: The demonstration shows that the subspace-search VQE protocol can be realized with photonic OAM qudits, validating the approach experimentally for the chosen test cases.
conclusion: Photonic OAM qudits are a viable platform for variational eigensolver demonstrations, though the work is primarily an applied quantum-algorithm implementation rather than a core information-theoretic or thermodynamic advance.
